cands.name: Chris Blackshear

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 80 since winning a January 2016 special election. Previously served on the Phenix City Council, including a stint as mayor pro tempore. Has also worked as a reporter covering Troy University football.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he came to Alabama. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, or policing. We found no land-use positions, controversies, foreign ties, or endorsements. The Ballotpedia page lists his sponsored bills only as an empty table, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022 or 2026. His work history beyond the City Council and the Troy football reporting is not described.

cands.name: Manfred Malone

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Manfred Malone is a Democrat who ran for Alabama House of Representatives District 80 in 2026 against incumbent Republican Chris Blackshear. No biographical or occupational details were found in the sources available.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists him as endorsed by two voter-guide groups: Tabitha's List (a Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (a Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Manfred Malone was born or raised, when he came to Alabama, or what work he has done. He has not held public office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign site statements, interviews or questionnaires. As a result, we have no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or land ownership. We found no controversies or foreign ties, but the sources were thin, so that is not a clean bill of health.

score.why: Raised $1,891, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation, work history or prior office could be found.
qual.why: The only page available covered the 2026 race and said nothing about his background, so no score is given.
